text:
Anya: Heads-up — we've had ~12 support tickets in the last 24h where EU customers on Enterprise tier saw their requests routed to `model-variant:fast-quant` fallback instead of `gptx-3b-highmem` during peak. Need better visibility in console: which requests triggered fallback and why. Can we show the routing decision in traces and add routing headers so customers can debug? Example log snippet attached in support thread.

Marta: ugh. do we know if this was capacity or policy? :thinking:

Anya: support says Dedicated pool in eu-west hit burst limit, smart-routing kicked in and used cheaper variant. We need per-request trace + header like `X-Redwood-Route: dedicated|fallback` and `X-Model-Variant: gptx-3b-highmem->fast-quant` so that support and customers can correlate.

Rahul: agree. We already add `X-Redwood-Alloc` for infra. Adding `X-Redwood-Route` + `X-RW-Model` is low-risk. Also should emit a span/tag in traces: `routing.decision` with reason enum {capacity_reached, policy_cost_cap, region_unavailable}. Sampling question — we can't trace every request, so add a debug header to force a sampled trace.

Sam: cost/telemetry: if we expose headers, also add metrics that count fallback occurrences by tenant, region, and reason. We can compute per-tenant fallback rate and trigger alerts when > 1% over 10m. Also tag cost delta so billing can show "tokens served by fallback variant".

Marta: UI: propose a small "Routing decisions" column in Request Trace view and a dashboard tile (bar chart) "Fallbacks by reason" with filters by tenant/region/model. Also allow clicking a trace to show headers panel.

Console-Bot: deploy pipeline `routing-headers` succeeded in staging (build #3729) :white_check_mark:

Rahul: implementation notes — runtime can annotate response headers in the proxy layer. For traces we'll add a tag on the root span and link to `route_id`. Sample curl header that support can use:

```
curl -i https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer <key>" \
  -H "X-Redwood-Debug: routing" \
  -d '{"model":"gptx-3b-highmem","input":"..."}'

# response headers will include:
# X-Redwood-Route: dedicated->fallback
# X-RW-Model: gptx-3b-highmem->fast-quant
# X-Redwood-Route-Reason: capacity_reached
```

Anya: Nice. Also need to store `route_reason` in request logs (not just traces) for historical dashboards; retention 30d for aggregated counts. Avoid PII.

Sam: quotas interaction: if fallback is due to quota on customer's dedicated pool, we should surface quota page link in trace UI and a tooltip explaining fallback. Also consider rate-limited badge on trace.

Marta: UX: rollout side — when we do canary shift of a model variant, console should show expected routing policy and a per-tenant "will I be affected?" preview. Maybe a little modal that shows e.g., "Your tenant (Enterprise-eu) will default to dedicated, but fallback triggers if burst%>80".

Rahul: quick infra checklist I'm adding to the PR: add header annotation, trace tag, metric counters (by tenant/region/reason/model), UI tile + trace headers panel, quota link. Also per-route sample size for traces (1 per 100 requests by default, higher for enterprise tenants).

Anya: timeline? We'll need support access to identify impacted customers for tickets ASAP.

Marta: I can prototype UI mock tomorrow. Rahul/Sam — can we get a staging rollout to EU region with header + metric before EOD? If yes I'll fast-track the mock.

Rahul: I'll push PR this morning, staging rollout in ~3h. Metrics will be live in staging after the job runs. Will add an opt-in header `X-Redwood-Debug: routing` to force sampling.

Support: can confirm that customers will use header to share traces. :thumbsup:

Sam: note — update billing docs to clarify fallback cost delta and how it appears in token-level cost breakdown.

Anya: sweet. please @me on PRs. thanks all.
